about.title: Personal Injury Help in Hemet, California
about.longDescription: Hemet is home to roughly 84,000 people, and most of its daily traffic funnels through a handful of wide, busy corridors. Public records from 2025 show 273 injury collisions inside city limits, with 419 people hurt and 7 lives lost. The largest share of those reports came from Florida Avenue, State Street, Stetson Avenue, and Sanderson Avenue — the same streets residents use to reach work, school, and the grocery store. The counts also tend to rise on Thursdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when the evening commute is heaviest. If you were injured in one of those collisions, or in a fall, a dog attack, or any other incident someone else caused, you may be weighing whether to talk to a lawyer at all. LawProactive exists to make that first step simpler. We are a free service, not a law firm. We do not give legal advice or handle cases ourselves. What we do is connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency — meaning there is no fee unless your case ends in a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing, and you are never obligated to hire anyone you speak with.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Hemet Claim

items.title: You Have Two Years, Usually
items.desc: California allows two years from the date of injury to file most personal injury claims. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share of the blame, but you are not shut out entirely.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not limit non-economic damages such as pain, emotional distress, or loss of enjoyment of life. An attorney can explain how these are documented.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency. You pay nothing up front, and legal fees come only from a settlement or verdict — if there is one.

items.question: Where do collisions most often happen in Hemet?
items.answer: Based strictly on public-record collision counts, the highest volumes in Hemet are reported along Florida Avenue, State Street, Stetson Avenue, and Sanderson Avenue. These are also among the city's busiest routes, so higher traffic naturally means more reports. Records also show crashes tending to peak on Thursdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date you were hurt. Claims against a government entity — for example, a crash involving a city vehicle or a fall on public property — can require a claim within six months. An attorney can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney. We do not practice law, give legal advice, or take a portion of your recovery.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the crash?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of responsibility, but you can still recover the remainder. Even someone found mostly at fault may still have a claim worth discussing.

items.question: What will it cost me to hire an attorney?
items.answer: Attorneys in our network work on a contingency basis, so there are no upfront fees. They are paid a percentage only if your case results in a recovery. If there is no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.
